content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (walk-away territory) — T4C**

- **What the document does:** Section 8.1 fixes a three-year term. All termination rights are cause-based: material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), Vendor security/service-level/legal/IP failure (9.3), plus remedy-specific exits in 6.2, 19.4 and 27.3. Section 9.4 is simply absent. Section 2.1 affirmatively locks Customer in — "take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights."
- **Why it fails fallback:** there is no Customer convenience right at any notice period in a multi-year term, and Section 2.1 expressly negates one. (Vendor also has no convenience right, but nothing in the text states this, so it is carried by the new clause rather than claimed as already met.)
- **Cure (preferred level, two operations):** a new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience exit over the Agreement or any Order Form with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term; plus a surgical conform of Section 2.1 that removes only the termination bar and expressly preserves the reduction restriction, so no contradictory retained mechanic survives.
- **Not double-flagged:** Section 8.2 renewal/non-renewal is a RENEWAL term and was left untouched.
